source.title: Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses cited work on neural networks fitting random noise, but its own experiments test NLP probes memorizing word type-to-label mappings, not the claim's random-label training behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper's control tasks assign a random output to each word type, so repeated tokens share labels. These are probe memorization results, not results on networks fitting independently randomized training-example labels. The cited result from Zhang et al. (2017) is not this paper's own result.
record.test_reason: Section 5.1 explicitly distinguishes its structured, word-type random mappings from Zhang et al.'s example-level random labels. Its own results report development accuracy and selectivity, not training-set interpolation of completely random labels. The distinction is the randomization unit and outcome measured, not the use of NLP rather than images.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's central paraphrase is accurate: probe accuracy reflects both representation information and probe expressivity; control tasks and selectivity help interpret this interaction. Dropout often fails to improve MLP selectivity, while selected alternative constraints help. The final scope statement should concern completely random example labels, rather than image labels specifically.
record.recipe_differences: NLP probe experiments on ELMo representations and word-type control tasks; not the original image-label randomization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe family, task, regularization and hyperparameters, and representation layer affect reported control-task accuracy or selectivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Probes achieve substantial development accuracy on random mappings shared across occurrences of each word type. Dropout does not consistently improve MLP selectivity; selected dimensionality constraints and weight decay can improve it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NLP probes can memorize structured random word-type mappings, with performance depending on probe capacity and regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Linguistic accuracy minus control accuracy varies across representations and probe families, including substantial part-of-speech selectivity differences despite similar linguistic accuracies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation comparisons based on linguistic probe accuracy can be confounded by differences in access to word identity and probe memorization capacity.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study reports development-set probe accuracies; uncertainty intervals are not stated. Results concern random word-type mappings for NLP probes, so they do not directly establish the claim's image-label setting.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 reports additional control-task outcomes across complexity-control settings, but values are presented only in plots and are not individually extracted. The table and text results above provide the numeric control-task outcomes and representation comparisons.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely randomized example labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Training-set interpolation of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance across label-corruption fractions.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent completely random-label interpolation, and whether removing regularizers harms true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels. Fixed-step stopping and sample-size comparisons do not establish that ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The Table 1 and Table 2 values are correctly transcribed. States are changed to cannot_determine relative to V1–V6; this does not dispute the reported probe outcomes. Section 2.3 explains that control-task development performance is bounded by training/evaluation word-type overlap plus chance performance on unseen types. These development results therefore measure a different construct from interpolation with chance generalization.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard deep networks fit independently randomized image labels, with test error at chance and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost and convergence rate as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
Training and test performance across increasing fractions of corrupted labels.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent random-label fitting or affect true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.
